thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-7831 fired: redis-prod-eu-west1 acceptqueue > 95% and pgbouncer waiters rising > 200
pagerduty: PD-7831 — High — redis-prod-eu-west1 acceptqueue saturation — https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD-7831
sara: I got the page, oncall responding. grabbing logs now.
mike: I see increased 5xx from api-gateway, likely DB timeouts. top-level symp: steady 500/s, p50 latency 800ms.
jana: Customer Success pinged — a few enterprise tenants reporting outages (in-app errors + webhook failures).
ops-oncall: quick context: earlier there was a large analytics backfill kicked off from batch-worker-3 around 09:12 UTC, looks like it targeted production by mistake. could be the culprit.
sara: Can we pause that job? who's the owner?
mike: owner is data-team's nightly-backfill job run by service data-mgr-1. I can kill the job from the controller: `kubectl -n batch delete job nightly-backfill-2026-03-15`
kevin: before killing, note the job holds long-running DB cursors — killing will free connections but might leave some transactions in 'idle in transaction'. I'll watch pg activity.
sara: do it. we need immediate relief.
mike: done — job delete issued. controller shows pods terminating.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-7831 acknowledged by sara at 1725554340
jana: checking redis: `redis-cli -h redis-prod-eu-west1 INFO Clients | grep blocked_clients` -> blocked_clients: 180
kevin: pgbouncer stats: `SHOW CLIENTS;` shows waiters=210, active=400, server_active=380, server_idle=10. pgbouncer pool exhaustion + long server-side queries.
ops-oncall: running quick health commands:
```
kubectl -n infra exec -it pgbouncer-0 -- psql -c "SHOW POOLS;"
# output: pool_count=48 waiters_total=212
```
sara: good — looks like deleting the job started freeing up new connections (pods gone), but acceptqueue still high. what's redis persistence/eviction doing?
mike: redis memory steady, but clients are piling up on acceptqueue. I'm going to rotate the app's connection timeout so slow requests get short-circuited. applying temporary config on api-gateway: `upstream_read_timeout 5s`
customer-success: heads-up: already received 7 tickets, two customers flagged severity-high. notifying account teams.
kevin: manual GC on a few app nodes might unblock futures holding DB conns. running `systemctl restart app-worker` on two worst hosts (eu-west1-a/b).
sara: also enable readonly fallback for web UI to reduce write traffic: flipping feature flag `ui_writes_enabled=false` for EU region.
ops-oncall: autoscale note: pgbouncer is not auto-scaling — it's static. I'm going to scale pgbouncer replicas from 3 -> 6 now.
mike: scaling pgbouncer replicas...
incident-bot: deploy-bot: scaling pgbouncer statefulset to 6 replicas initiated by ops-oncall
sara: after scaling a few things: redis blocked_clients -> 60, pgbouncer waiters -> 90. still high but trending down.
jana: customer impact update: about ~15% of API requests for write-heavy endpoints are 500-ing or 502-ing; read endpoints largely degraded but functional.
kevin: I'm seeing a few lingering `idle in transaction` connections on pg-primary. running `SELECT pid, state, query_start, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY query_start DESC LIMIT 20;`
kevin: found several stuck queries from nightly-backfill; manually terminating pids for the oldest ones (pg_terminate_backend). terminated 8 pids.
mike: connection counts are dropping, pgbouncer server_idle increasing to 120, active down to 220.
sara: good. let's mute noisy PD alerts to avoid escalation storm: silencing PD alert group for 10m.
incident-bot: pagerduty: PD-7831 silenced for 10 minutes by sara
jana: ticket churn: CS opened an incident post to impacted customers and added a note that team is actively mitigating, ETA unknown.
ops-oncall: recommendation: add immediate rate-limit for the analytics job controller to prevent accidental prod runs: add `service.account: batch-runner` constraint + require prod flag. file a follow-up.
sara: mitigation checklist so far: kill backfill job, terminate stuck pg queries, restart hot app workers, scale pgbouncer, enable readonly UI, short upstream timeouts, silence PD, CS notified.
kevin: verifying no replication lag and no background wal bloat. replication lag normal.
mike: one leftover symptom: a small number of webhooks to customers failed and are queued for retry; that's expected until backlog drains.
customer-success: noted — we'll monitor and provide customers a follow-up status update in 30m.
sara: moving to handoff: I'm going to keep watch for 15m then hand to infra rotation. any objections?
jana: fine with me. runbook step: file an incident postmortem with timeline + root cause (human-triggered prod backfill) and corrective actions (controller guards, PD routing change).
ops-oncall: I'll own postmortem and the follow-up ticket to make backfill jobs require an env-lock and safety check.
kevin: logging action: add a metric for 'batch-job-triggered-in-prod' to alert earlier.
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-7831 resolved by sara at 1725554698 — condition cleared (acceptqueue < 10%, waiters < 20)
sara: closing loop: systems stabilized, p50 back to 120ms, errors down to baseline. leaving notes in the incident channel. handing to ops-oncall for monitoring and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
ops-oncall: acked handoff, will keep a 1h watch and draft the postmortem.
customer-success: will close customer-facing incidents once we confirm retry success for webhooks.
sara: great work team. follow-ups: (1) infra ticket to prevent prod backfill accidental triggers, (2) pgbouncer autoscale exploration, (3) add early-warning metric for large batch triggers.
mike: uploading logs + query dumps to the incident folder: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-7831/logs
kevin: tagging folks for postmortem: @data-team @infra @platform-security
jana: extra note: add a playbook section for 'kill runaway batch jobs' with safe kill steps (how to check for idle-in-transaction, when to terminate backend vs draining).
sara: thanks — thread closed when ops-oncall marks postmortem draft ready.
